summary: Session set harvester-manifest-index-and-batch-readiness completed all 4 sessions (Final) and closed every finding the first real downstream consumer raised when running AccessHarvester run against NorthwindDevEdition.accdb on 2026-05-29 (the same day Phase 4 closed and v1.0.0 cut). Session 1 fixed Finding #1 (manifest omitting Tables/Relationships/Modules) by populating the call site in Pipeline.cs that constructed DatabaseManifestAggregator without the typed collections, root-caused the Modules-empty case independently, added the ManifestCompletenessTests per-category invariant test, and regenerated both committed goldens; three pre-existing schema-vs-typed-record drifts that surfaced once the empty arrays got populated were deferred to Session 2's planned v1.1 bump per user direction. Session 2 closed Finding #2 (manifest is not a navigation index) by adding a top-level FileMap (per-category {count, glob} records), a top-level Documentation block (public HTTPS URL to interpretation-guide.md + the schema version), and a static READ-ME-FIRST.md emitted alongside manifest.json. The same session shipped the additive harvester-schema v1.0 to v1.1 bump with per-document schema dispatch in RunValidate (both schemas embedded, cached per version; --json-status grew SupportedSchemaVersions[] + PerManifestSchemaVersion[]), absorbing Session 1's three schema drifts plus a fourth corrective (LateBound enum value missing from Classification.Purity — the actual root cause of Session 1's 1099-error cascade). Session 3 closed Findings #4 and #6 plus the optional cross-DB roll-up index: --no-clean wiring with default-clean per-tier semantics; HarvesterVersion/StartedAt/DurationMs/Clean provenance on the --json-status envelope (non-deterministic fields excluded from the determinism gate the same way ExportedAt is); cross-DB roll-up emitted at <out>/AccessMetaData/index.json at the end of every Pipeline.Run with the public EmitRootIndex entry point for batch drivers; centralization of HarvesterVersion resolution into a single canonical DatabaseManifest.ResolveHarvesterVersion() helper (in response to a R1 Major finding about manifest-vs-envelope version drift). Session 4 closed Findings #3 (per-field-type semantics in interpretation-guide.md §5.5 — DAO type-code table from 1 through 23 plus 101 Attachment and the 102-109 multi-valued family, mapped to TypeCode/TypeName/Attributes/DDL representation with Northwind's Employees.Attachments as the worked example, plus prose on Hyperlink-vs-Memo via Attributes & 0x8000, AutoNumber, Lookup, multi-valued, and validation rules/defaults) and #5 (new batch-operations guide at docs/harvester/batch-operations.md covering the multi-DB layout, sequential-only operation, MSACCESS/RCW hygiene across runs, --clean/--no-clean semantics, the cross-DB roll-up index, and the status-envelope provenance fields with a determinism column). The batch-operations doc is wired into install.md, the interpretation guide's §10, and docs/README.md under a new Running the harvester subsection. Test posture at close: 400 Resolver + 70 SymbolDb + 689 Pipeline + 452 AccessHarvester = 1611 hermetic tests pass; 2 pre-existing synthetic-fixture skips. Integration suite: 53/56 in the full sequential dotnet test run; the three failures (CliExtract/CliRun/CliTranslate against HomeHealthCare.accdb at 60s timeout) are the documented xUnit parallel-COM contention pattern Session 3's notes flagged for ClassifyCommandTests, with the victim rotating across runs. All three pass cleanly in isolation (dotnet test --filter for the three tests completed in 33s); mitigation is the scope of the recommended next session set (harvester-parallel-com-test-cleanup). Total set routed cost ~$1.09 across the four sessions (S1 $0.13 + S2 $0.18 + S3 $0.40 + S4 $0.3818: R1 gpt-5-4 session-verification $0.2738 surfaced one Major closeout-placeholder finding plus two Minor doc-accuracy findings (DDL fallback rows for BINARY/TEXT/VARBINARY/CHAR omitted the unsized spellings; dbVariableField hex value 0x00000001 was wrong — correct is 0x00000002, 0x00000001 is dbFixedField); all three fixed in-session and R2 gpt-5-4 VERIFIED for $0.1052; plus gemini-pro next-set analysis $0.0028). The set ships every gap the first real downstream consumer hit: a binary-only consumer that opens <out>/AccessMetaData/index.json cold can now discover every harvested DB, traverse its manifest.json, follow the schema-version-stamped Documentation.Url to the interpretation guide, read the per-category FileMap.<Category>.Glob to find the per-object IR files, and run the harvester safely across hundreds of DBs in one batch per the new batch-operations guide.

next_session_set.summary: Close the documented xUnit parallel-COM contention pattern in the Integration test suite. The flake manifests as 60s timeouts on whichever CLI test class wins the bad slot at the same time another class drives MSACCESS against the same .accdb (Session 3 saw ClassifyCommandTests; Session 4 saw CliExtract/CliRun/CliTranslate). Mitigation: xUnit Collection serialisation across COM-using CLI test classes, or pre-staged inputs replacing chained classify-driven setup. Recommended orchestrator: claude sonnet-4.6 @ effort=medium per the routed gemini-pro analysis on 2026-05-29 — maintenance-mode work, mechanical implementation, no synthesis. Estimated routed cost band: Low (<$0.50). Currently a stub (no spec); author the spec as part of the set.
